questions.text: Explain the legislative powers and functions of the state legislature.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the legislative powers and functions of the state legislature. (A)

answer.value:
Legislative Powers and Functions of the State Legislature
An ordinary bill can be introduced in either house of the state legislature.
Bills passed by the Legislative Assembly are sent to the Legislative Council for approval. The Council must return the bill with or without amendments within three months. If not, the Assembly sends the bill again, and the Council must approve it within one month. Otherwise, it is deemed approved by both houses and sent to the Governor for assent.
The Legislative Council can delay an ordinary bill for up to four months but has no further authority.

questions.text: Explain the financial powers and functions of the Governor.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the financial powers and functions of the Governor. (A)

answer.value:
Financial Powers and Functions of the Governor
A financial bill cannot be introduced in the Legislative Assembly without the Governor’s prior approval.
The Governor has the authority to establish the State Finance Commission and the State Planning Board.
The Governor can release funds from the state’s contingency fund to address emergencies like drought, floods, or earthquakes.
The state’s consolidated fund is under the Governor’s control.

questions.text_as_printed: Describe the discretionary powers of the Governor. (A)

Discretionary Powers of the Governor
The Governor can reserve a bill passed by the legislature for the President’s assent.
In case of a constitutional crisis or failure in the state, the Governor can report to the President and recommend President’s Rule.
The Governor can dismiss a Council of Ministers that has lost the confidence of the Legislative Assembly.

questions.text: List the financial powers and functions of the state legislature.
questions.text_as_printed: List the financial powers and functions of the state legislature. (A)

answer.value:
Financial Powers and Functions of the State Legislature
The Legislative Assembly has more financial authority than the Legislative Council.
As per the Constitution, a financial bill must be introduced in the Legislative Assembly.
A financial bill approved by the Legislative Assembly is sent to the Legislative Council for approval.
The Council must return the bill with its approval within 14 days; otherwise, it is deemed approved by both houses and sent to the Governor for assent.
The Legislative Council can delay a financial bill for up to 14 days but has no further financial authority.

questions.text: Explain the legislative powers and functions of the Governor.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the legislative powers and functions of the Governor. (A)

answer.value:
Legislative Powers and Functions of the Governor
The Governor has the authority to summon and prorogue the sessions of the state legislature.
The Governor can dissolve the Legislative Assembly on the recommendation of the Chief Minister.
The Governor nominates one-sixth of the Legislative Council members based on their contributions to arts, literature, science, social service, or cooperative movements.
The Governor can assent to, return for reconsideration, or reject a bill passed by the legislature, or reserve it for the President’s assent if necessary.

Formulates and implements state policies.

Each minister ensures the efficient functioning of their department.
Supervises and coordinates the activities of various departments.

questions.text: Explain structure of the Legislative Assembly.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain structure of the Legislative Assembly. (E)

answer.value:
The Legislative Assembly is the lower house of the State Legislature.
The number of seats depends on the population of the state.
Maximum number of seats: 500, Minimum: 60.
Smaller states have fewer seats (e.g., Sikkim has 32 members).
The Karnataka Legislative Assembly currently has 224 elected members.
Earlier, it had 225 members including one nominated Anglo-Indian member.
The 104th Constitutional Amendment Act (2020) removed the Anglo-Indian nomination.
In Karnataka, 36 seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes and 15 for Scheduled Tribes.

questions.text: Mention the composition and functions of the Legislative Council.
questions.text_as_printed: Mention the composition and functions of the Legislative Council. (A)

answer.value:
Formation and Functions of the Legislative Council
The upper house of the state legislature is called the Legislative Council.
Its membership cannot exceed one-third of the Legislative Assembly’s membership and must not be less than 40 members.
Karnataka’s Legislative Council has 75 members.
Members represent five constituencies: elected by Legislative Assembly members, local bodies, graduates, teachers, and nominated by the Governor for contributions in arts, science, literature, social service, or cooperative movements.
The term of the Legislative Council is 6 years, and it cannot be dissolved prematurely, earning it the title of a permanent house.

questions.text: Explain the powers and functions of the Chief Minister.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the powers and functions of the Chief Minister. (A)

answer.value:
Powers and Functions of the Chief Minister
Recommends the formation of the Council of Ministers to the Governor.
Recommends the allocation and transfer of portfolios to ministers.
Can recommend the dismissal of disloyal ministers to the Governor.
As the head of the government, plays a key role in policy formulation.
Chairs, convenes, and prorogues meetings of the Council of Ministers.
Oversees the efficiency of various departments and ensures coordination.
Can recommend the dissolution of the Legislative Assembly to the Governor.
Acts as a link between the Governor and the Council of Ministers and advises on appointments to various posts.
